en.title: Rounds of Sequential Scanning to Process Packages in Order
en.description:
You are given a permutation of 1..n. In each round, scan from left to right and process the next not-yet-processed number as soon as you reach it; several numbers can be processed in a row within one round. Find how many rounds are needed to process all numbers.

The standard I/O and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..1000000), and the second line contains a permutation of 1..n.
en.explanation: Example 1: the first round processes 1, 2; the second 3, 4; the third 5, so the answer is 3. Example 2: a single scan finishes. Example 3: each round can process only one number, so the answer is 3.
hints: Record the position of each number. One round is needed to start; every time pos[v+1]<pos[v], a new scan is required, adding one round.
